description: A WRITE that writes its [ retry-phrase ] [ WITH LOCK | WITH NO LOCK ] pair AFTER its AT END-OF-PAGE / NOT AT END-OF-PAGE phrases. ISO/IEC 1989:2002 Format 1 (sequential) prints ADVANCING, then the END-OF-PAGE bracket, then [ retry-phrase ], then WITH LOCK / WITH NO LOCK (§2002:14.8.47.1, measured on the rendered PDF page 580); the 2014 Format 1 moves the pair before the END-OF-PAGE phrases (§2014:14.9.47.1), which 2023 keeps (§2023:14.9.51.2); ISO/IEC 1989:2014 Annex E.2 item 29 records the move as a substantive change potentially affecting existing programs (§2014:E.2: "Through an editorial error, the LOCK and RETRY phrases were placed in an incorrect location in the syntax diagram for the sequential format of the WRITE statement" ... "This only affects programs that contain sequential-format WRITE statements with both a LOCK or a RETRY phrase and an AT EOP or NOT AT EOP phrase"). So the 2002 place is in no later format: COBOL0902 from 2014 (an error strict, a warning under --permissive with the phrases bound as written). Below 2002 neither phrase exists (the RETRY and record-lock rows refuse them). The grammar parses the pair in either place as one retryLockPhrases element and VersionConformancePass.ParseArm.GateRetryLockPlace asks which place was written (kb/Work PB5620).
display: the retry or WITH LOCK phrase of a WRITE written after its END-OF-PAGE phrases
vcr: VCR Table 7 row 7.79 (§2014:E.2 item 29; kb/Work PB5620)
source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. VMWLA02.
ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION.
FILE-CONTROL.
    SELECT LPF ASSIGN TO "vmwla02.prt" ORGANIZATION SEQUENTIAL
        LOCK MODE IS MANUAL.
DATA DIVISION.
FILE SECTION.
FD LPF LINAGE IS 2 LINES.
01 P-REC PIC X(4).
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    OPEN OUTPUT LPF
    WRITE P-REC AFTER ADVANCING 1 LINE
        AT END-OF-PAGE DISPLAY "EOP"
        WITH LOCK
    END-WRITE
    CLOSE LPF
    STOP RUN.
